title: IFEVAL-RESPONSE-ORACLE: with an executed per-response constraint-checker vector attached to each trace, does the IFEval judge's INDECISION collapse (COULD-NOT-VERIFY) or persist (WOULD-NOT-COMMIT)? (judged, 1,628 calls under plan Amendment 9; a decisiveness-and-obedience instrument, never a rung of the reference ladder)
question: GEN-ARENA's IFEval cell failed as much by refusing to commit as by being wrong (accuracy 0.658, decidable ties 0.256, flips 0.380, against MATH's 0.935 / 0.055 / 0.237). Does handing the judge the executed checker's per-response PASS/FAIL vector collapse the ties and flips (COULD-NOT-VERIFY) or leave them standing while accuracy jumps (WOULD-NOT-COMMIT)? The name is not CHECKER-OUTPUT: the IFEVAL RULING of 2026-09-23 establishes that IFEval has no question-level checker output, so what is attached is a per-response ORACLE and the ladder's IFEval rung stays at SPECIFICATION 0.658 permanently whatever this test reads.

sentence_of_record: On the IFEval reserved side, attaching an EXECUTED per-response constraint-checker vector to each trace collapsed the deployed judge's indecision: on the same 407 key-decidable matches over 122 questions, judged in one interleaved session, the decidable tie rate fell from 0.263 to 0.012 (-25.1pp, discordant 5 against 107, exact McNemar p < 1e-25) and the flip rate from 0.243 to 0.012 (-23.1pp, 5 against 99, p < 1e-23), while convention-A accuracy rose from 0.654 to 0.988 [0.976, 0.998] question-clustered (paired: 136 matches repaired, 0 broken). GEN-ARENA's IFEval cell is COULD-NOT-VERIFY, not WOULD-NOT-COMMIT: the judge failed to count the constraints, not to commit. plain_description.what: On instruction-following questions (IFEval), judges the same 407 matches twice: once normally, and once with the automatic constraint checker's pass/fail result for each response attached. It then compares tie rate, order flips and accuracy. Uses 1,628 judge calls.
plain_description.why: The judge did poorly on IFEval (many ties and flips). This tests whether it could not check the constraints or simply would not commit to a verdict.
plain_description.information: If ties vanish once checking is done for the judge, the problem is verification; if ties persist, the judge is unwilling to decide. Result: ties fell from 26% to 1%, flips from 24% to 1%, and accuracy rose from 0.65 to 0.99. So the judge failed to count constraints, not to commit. Important limit: the attached result decides the answer outright. This is an upper bound, not a usable recipe, and it is from one judge, one session and one corpus.
